 PRESS RELEASE
 EXHIBIT 99.1 
 Nutanix Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results 
 Reports 15% YoY ARR Growth and Solid Free Cash Flow 
 Nutanix Announces CEO Succession Plan; Board Initiates Search for Next CEO 
 SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nutanix, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTNX), a hybrid cloud leader and AI platform company, today announced financial results for its first quarter ended October 31, 2026.
 “In the first quarter we delivered results that exceeded all of our guided metrics,” said Rajiv Ramaswami, CEO of Nutanix. “We also continued to invest in our cloud platform, especially with respect to AI and broadening our support for external storage.”
 “Our first quarter results demonstrated a good balance of top and bottom line performance with 15% year-over-year ARR growth and solid free cash flow generation,” said Rukmini Sivaraman, CFO of Nutanix. “We remain focused on delivering sustainable growth and improving profitability.”
 Nutanix today separately announced that the Board is working with Chief Executive Officer Rajiv Ramaswami to identify and recruit his successor, and he will step down after his successor has been appointed and assumes the role. Ramaswami will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the Company for a period of time after his successor is in place to ensure a smooth transition. The Board has engaged a leading national search firm to assist the process of identifying Nutanix’s next CEO.

 Recent Company Highlights 
 Nutanix Receives Micron Global Supplier Award for IT & Professional Services: Nutanix announced it was honored with the Outstanding Supplier Performance Award in IT & Professional Services at Micron Supplier Day 2026.
 Nutanix Builds a Faster Foundation for Production AI: Nutanix expanded its AI ecosystem with NVIDIA, Supermicro, and Netris to help enterprises and service providers quickly deploy and scale production AI, and reduce AI costs.
 Nutanix Acquires Ryax Technologies to Help Customers Accelerate Agentic AI Initiatives: Nutanix completed its acquisition of Ryax Technologies, an AI-driven compute orchestration and management platform company, and plans to integrate the platform’s advanced GPU utilization and smart scheduling capabilities into Nutanix Kubernetes Platform (NKP) and Nutanix Enterprise AI (NAI).
 Nutanix Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Server Virtualization Platforms: Nutanix announced its recognition as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Server Virtualization Platforms.
 Nutanix Named a Leader in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Distributed Hybrid Infrastructure: Nutanix announced its recognition as a Leader in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Distributed Hybrid Infrastructure.
 Nutanix Recognized in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Container Management for Second Consecutive Year: Nutanix announced its recognition as a Challenger in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Container Management for the second consecutive year, following the 2024 launch of NKP.

 Footnotes 
 1 Annual Recurring Revenue , or ARR , is defined as the sum of ACV for all subscription contracts from all customers in effect as of the end of a specific period, assuming any subscription contract that expires is renewed on its existing terms. ARR excludes the value of professional services, non-portable software and support contracts and hardware sales. For the purposes of this calculation, we generally assume that the contract term begins on the date when the software is made available to the customer. ACV is defined as the total annualized value of a contract. The total annualized value for a contract is calculated by dividing the total value of the contract by the number of years in the term of such contract. 
 2 Average Contract Duration represents the dollar-weighted term, calculated on a billings basis, across all subscription contracts, as well as our limited number of life-of-device contracts, using an assumed term of five years for life-of-device licenses, executed in the period. 
 3 Weighted average share count used in computing diluted non-GAAP net income per share. 
 Non-GAAP Financial Measures and Other Key Performance Measures 
 To supplement our consolidated financial statements, which are prepared and presented in accordance with GAAP, this press release includes the following non-GAAP financial and other key performance measures: non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, free cash flow, Annual Recurring Revenue (or ARR), and Average Contract Duration. In computing non-GAAP financial measures, we exclude certain items such as stock-based compensation, costs associated with our acquisitions (such as amortization of acquired intangible assets and other acquisition-related costs), restructuring charges, litigation costs related to certain litigation matters, the amortization of the debt discount and issuance costs related to debt, interest expense related to debt, changes in the fair value of convertible notes receivable, valuation allowance releases, and other non-recurring transactions and the related tax impact. Non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, and non-GAAP operating margin are financial measures which we believe provide useful information to investors because they provide meaningful supplemental information regarding our performance and liquidity by excluding certain expenses and expenditures such as stock-based compensation expense that may not be indicative of our ongoing core business operating results. Free cash flow is a performance measure that we believe provides useful information to our management and investors about the amount of cash generated by the business after capital expenditures, and we define free cash flow as net cash provided by operating activities less purchases of property and equipment. ARR is a performance measure that we believe provides useful information to our management and investors as it allows us to better track the top-line growth of our subscription business (including our ability to acquire subscriptions with new customers and to retain and expand with existing customers), while normalizing for differences in contract durations. Our calculation of ARR is not adjusted for the impact of any known or projected future events (such as customer cancellations, expansion or contraction of existing customer relationships or price increases or decreases) that may cause any subscription contract not to be renewed on its existing terms. ARR is a performance measure that should be viewed independently of revenue and does not represent our revenue under GAAP on an annualized basis or a forecast of GAAP revenue. Investors should not place undue reliance on ARR as an indicator of our future or expected results. ARR does not have any standardized meaning and is therefore unlikely to be comparable to similarly titled performance measures presented by other companies. We use these non-GAAP financial and key performance measures for financial and operational decision-making and as a means to evaluate period-to-period comparisons. However, these non-GAAP financial and key performance measures have limitations as analytical tools and you should not consider them in isolation or as substitutes for analysis of our results as reported under GAAP. Non-GAAP gross margin, non-GAAP operating expenses, non-GAAP operating income, non-GAAP operating margin, and free cash flow are not substitutes for gross margin, operating expenses, operating income, operating margin, and net cash provided by operating activities, respectively. There is no GAAP measure that is comparable to ARR or Average Contract Duration, so we have not reconciled the ARR or Average Contract Duration data included in this press release to any GAAP measure. In addition, other companies, including companies in our industry, may calculate non-GAAP financial measures and key performance measures differently or may use other measures to evaluate their performance, all of which could reduce the usefulness of our non-GAAP financial measures and key performance measures as tools for comparison. We urge you to review the reconciliation of our non-GAAP financial measures and key performance measures to the most directly comparable GAAP financial measures included below in the tables captioned “Reconciliation of GAAP to Non-GAAP Profit Measures” and “Reconciliation of GAAP Net Cash Provided By Operating Activities to Non-GAAP Free Cash Flow,” and not to rely on any single financial measure to evaluate our business. This press release also includes the following forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures as part of our second quarter fiscal 2027 outlook and/or our fiscal 2027 outlook: non-GAAP operating margin and free cash flow. We are unable to reconcile these forward-looking non-GAAP financial measures to their most directly comparable GAAP financial measures without unreasonable efforts, as we are currently unable to predict with a reasonable degree of certainty the type and extent of certain items that would be expected to impact the GAAP financial measures for these periods but would not impact the non-GAAP financial measures.

 EXHIBIT 99.2 
 Nutanix Announces CEO Succession Plan 
 Board Working with CEO Rajiv Ramaswami to Identify and Recruit Successor to Lead the Company into its Next Phase of Growth 
 Ramaswami to Continue as CEO Until Successor is Appointed and Assumes the Role 
 SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nutanix, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTNX ), a hybrid cloud leader and AI platform company, today announced that the Board is working with Chief Executive Officer Rajiv Ramaswami to identify and recruit his successor, and he will step down after his successor has been appointed and assumes the role. Ramaswami will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the Company for a period of time after his successor is in place to ensure a smooth transition.
 The Board has engaged a leading national search firm to assist in identifying Nutanix's next CEO – a leader who will accelerate the company’s next phase of growth as it builds on its leadership in hybrid multicloud infrastructure and expands its role as a platform for enterprise AI.
 “As CEO, Rajiv has had a tremendous impact on Nutanix’s business, and we deeply appreciate his leadership over the past six years,” said Virginia Gambale, Chair of the Board of Nutanix. “During his tenure, Rajiv led the Company’s transformation to subscription software, built a loyal and expanding global enterprise customer base, and established a technology portfolio that we believe positions us well for the AI era. The Board is focused on selecting an exceptional leader who can build on that foundation. We are grateful for his commitment to ensuring a smooth transition, which will provide continuity while we undertake that process.”
 “It has been a privilege to lead Nutanix and the remarkable team that has built this company,” said Rajiv Ramaswami. “Over the past six years, we transformed Nutanix into a growing and profitable cloud software business and laid the groundwork for its evolution as an AI infrastructure platform. Nutanix is a much stronger company today, and I am proud of everything the team has accomplished together. I am committed to supporting the Board through its search process and ensuring a smooth handoff to Nutanix’s next leader.”
 Ramaswami’s email to employees regarding this announcement can be found here .
 Separately today, Nutanix announced its financial results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027. For additional information regarding the Company’s financial results and outlook, please see Nutanix’s first quarter fiscal 2027 earnings release issued today.
 Forward-Looking Statements 
 This press release contains express and implied forward-looking statements, including, but not limited to, statements regarding the Company’s CEO succession process, including the search for and appointment of a successor Chief Executive Officer and the timing of the leadership transition; Mr. Ramaswami’s expected continued service as Chief Executive Officer during the succession process and expected service as a senior advisor following the transition; the Company’s ability to achieve a smooth leadership transition and maintain leadership continuity; and the Company’s strategy, growth opportunities, competitive position and opportunities relating to hybrid multicloud infrastructure and enterprise AI. These forward-looking statements are not historical facts and are instead based on Nutanix’s current expectations, estimates and beliefs. The accuracy of such statements involves risks and uncertainties and depends upon future events, including those that may be beyond Nutanix’s control, and actual results may differ materially and adversely from those anticipated or implied by such statements, including, but not limited to: the Company’s ability to identify, recruit and successfully transition to a successor Chief Executive Officer on the anticipated timeline; potential disruption or uncertainty resulting from the leadership transition, including with respect to the Company’s employees, customers, partners and business operations; the Company’s ability to retain and motivate key personnel during the succession process; the Company’s ability to successfully execute its strategy and capitalize on its market opportunities; changes in competitive dynamics, market opportunities or customer demand; and other risks as detailed in Nutanix’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended July 31, 2026 filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission, or the SEC, on September 18, 2026 and subsequent filings with the SEC, which should be read in conjunction with this press release.  Item 5.02. Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. 
 Chief Executive Officer Transition 
 On November 24, 2026, the Company announced that Rajiv Ramaswami, the Company’s Chief Executive Officer and a member of the Company’s Board of Directors (the “Board”), will step down as Chief Executive Officer and as a director of the Company. Mr. Ramaswami will continue to serve in those positions until the earlier of (i) the date on which the Company’s successor Chief Executive Officer commences employment with the Company and (ii) April 30, 2027 (the “Separation Date”). The Board has initiated a search process to identify the Company’s next Chief Executive Officer.
 In connection with the planned transition, on November 24, 2026, the Company and Mr. Ramaswami entered into a Transition Agreement and Release (the “Transition Agreement”). During the period through the Separation Date (the “Transition Period”), Mr. Ramaswami will continue to receive his current base salary, continue to vest in his outstanding equity awards in accordance with their terms, and remain eligible to participate in the Company’s employee benefit plans, subject to the terms and conditions of such plans. Mr. Ramaswami has agreed to continue performing the duties and responsibilities of Chief Executive Officer and to provide transition services as reasonably requested by the Board during the Transition Period. Upon the Separation Date, Mr. Ramaswami will cease to be an employee and director of the Company and will resign from all other positions he then holds with the Company and its subsidiaries. Following the Separation Date, subject to his timely execution and non-revocation of the Advisor Services Agreement and Release in the form attached to the Transition Agreement (the “Advisor Agreement”), Mr. Ramaswami will serve as an independent contractor advisor to the Company through September 30, 2027, unless earlier terminated pursuant to its terms. Under the Advisor Agreement, Mr. Ramaswami will provide transition and strategic advisory services to the Board and the Company’s successor Chief Executive Officer and will remain reasonably available to provide such services upon reasonable request. Subject to the terms and conditions of the Advisor Agreement, Mr. Ramaswami will be entitled to receive (i) a monthly advisory fee of $133,333 through September 30, 2027, (ii) payment of the cost of COBRA coverage through December 31, 2027 or, if earlier, until Mr. Ramaswami obtains other executive employment, and (iii) continued vesting of his outstanding equity awards in accordance with their existing terms through September 30, 2027, other than Mr. Ramaswami’s supplemental performance-based equity award granted in January 2024, which will terminate on the Separation Date in accordance with its terms. Mr. Ramaswami will also be eligible to receive a cash transition award of $5.0 million (the “Transition Award”), which will become payable following September 30, 2027, subject to specified service, leadership-transition and successor-onboarding conditions, the condition that Mr. Ramaswami not be employed in an executive capacity elsewhere through September 30, 2027, and his timely execution of the applicable release agreement. The conditions applicable to the Transition Award include continued availability and timely performance of the advisory services, achievement of specified leadership-transition and successor-onboarding milestones, assistance with the Company’s annual operating plan and special projects as requested, documented knowledge transfer, customer, partner and management handoffs, and support for executive-team continuity. If Mr. Ramaswami becomes employed in an executive capacity elsewhere before the completion of the advisory term, he will not be eligible to receive the Transition Award and the Company’s obligation to pay his COBRA premiums will cease. Such employment will not, by itself, affect his entitlement to his monthly advisory fee or continued equity vesting. If the Company terminates Mr. Ramaswami’s employment before the date on which his employment otherwise would have ended under the planned transition other than for cause, or terminates the Advisor Agreement before September 30, 2027 other than for cause, Mr. Ramaswami will remain entitled to the advisory fees that otherwise would have been payable through September 30, 2027, continued COBRA benefits through the applicable period, continued or accelerated treatment of certain equity awards through September 30, 2027, and the Transition Award, subject to the applicable release requirements.  Each RSU represents a contingent right to receive one share of the Company’s Class A common stock upon vesting. The RSUs will vest in 16 equal quarterly installments, with the first quarterly installment to vest on December 15, 2026, subject to continued service to the Company through each vesting date.
 Each PRSU represents a contingent right to receive one share of the Company’s Class A common stock upon vesting, provided that the actual number of PRSUs eligible to vest may be more or less than the target number of PRSUs. The PRSUs will be eligible to vest in up to three installments based on the total shareholder return of the Company (“Company TSR”) during each of the following performance periods (each, a “Performance Period”) relative to the total shareholder return of companies in the Nasdaq Composite Index (the “Indexed Companies”): (i) August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2027 (“Performance Period One”); (ii) August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2028 (“Performance Period Two”); and (iii) August 1, 2026 to July 31, 2029 (“Performance Period Three”). PRSUs that become eligible to vest based on performance for a Performance Period vest on September 15 following the Performance Period, subject to continued service to the Company through the vesting date.
 The number of PRSUs eligible to vest for each Performance Period will be determined based on an achievement percentage (the “Achievement Percentage”), which may range from 0% to 200%, except that the Achievement Percentage is capped at 100% for Performance Period One and Performance Period Two. Up to one-third of the target number of PRSUs will be eligible to vest as a result of performance for each of Performance Period One and Performance Period Two. The Achievement Percentage is (i) 0% if Company TSR ranks below the 25th percentile of the Indexed Companies, (ii) 50% if Company TSR ranks at the 25th percentile of the Indexed Companies, (iii) 100% if Company TSR ranks at the 50th percentile of the Indexed Companies, and (iv) 200% if Company TSR ranks at the 75th percentile of the Indexed Companies. If Company TSR ranks between these percentile thresholds, the Achievement Percentage is determined using linear interpolation. With respect to Performance Period Three, the number of PRSUs eligible to vest will equal the product of the Achievement Percentage and the full target number of PRSUs, less any PRSUs that already vested with respect to Performance Period One and Performance Period Two.
